summary: Deploy the new Saleor version without applying its migration (state_only), keep the note column while the old version continues to serve traffic, retire the old version, then drop the note column in a contract SQL stage after retire_old. This ensures no write conflict during overlap and removes the column only after the old version is gone.
write_consistency: During the overlap the old version continues to write notes into the note column; the new version omits the note field from its Django model and GraphQL inputs, so its INSERT/UPDATE statements never reference the column. No conflict arises because the new version never writes to note. After retire_old the old version stops, and the contract stage removes the column.

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version; after this only the new version runs.
Remove the note column from the account_user table.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
